s3 structural: re-verified s2 floor (136), improved to 130 via inlined base-address expr, and CONFIRMED H4's pass attribution (combine.c fold blocked by shared SS_SCORE_FLAG re-derivation liveness) vi

s5 permuter: objdump-diffed target vs the insn-exact bank_off chassis, found target caches BOTH bank_ptr AND a1_off as separate hard regs; a directed permuter campaign on that chassis plateaued 8332-9

s5 enumerate: exhaustive 16-spelling sweep of the base/key preamble (tools/spelling_enum.py) ties the banked 130 floor but finds no improvement — class-kills the preamble's spelling space and sharpens
Four-session 130 plateau broken to 10 (199 vs 200 insns): the never-run full objdump diff showed 12 of the 13 surplus instructions were source-level divergences, not register allocation.

frontier.hypothesis: H5 - the last missing instruction is target's second live copy of param a0 (`addu $a3,$a0,$zero`): target reads $a3/$a1 for every key build in a call-free block and $s5/$s4 for every one after a call, while our build has only the $s5/$s4 copies and reads the incoming $a0 directly. All six remaining register-name diffs and both unfilled delay slots follow from this one split.
frontier.mechanism: UNREAD - do not guess. Two live pseudos for one parameter is a local-alloc.c / global.c allocno question (possibly caller-save.c); the dump names the pass in one read.
frontier.next_probe: `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 _SsSndCrescendo` with the banked s6 candidate applied; read .greg/.lreg for the pseudo(s) carrying param a0 and compare the allocno count and conflict lists against the target's $a3/$s5 split. Then, only if the dump points at it, try parameter typing (s32 a0 / s32 a1, updating the forward decl at src/main.c:234 and the call site at main.c:285 - and re-measure SsSeqCalledTbyT, which that change also affects).

frontier.hypothesis: H6 - a directed permuter campaign is viable for the first time on this function: the s6 chassis is insn-count-near-exact (199 vs 200) with a purely register/scheduling residual, unlike the s4 campaign which ran on a 139-score chassis still carrying five unfixed source-level errors and plateaued 8332-9589 over 4687 iterations.
frontier.mechanism: n/a - search, not a named pass
frontier.next_probe: build a single-function permuter workspace from memory/grind/_SsSndCrescendo/candidate.c (the s6 body) and run a fresh-seed campaign per the fresh-seed stopping rule, waiting in-turn with `python3 tools/permuter_campaign.py wait --dir <ws>` and harvesting + stopping before the turn ends.

frontier.hypothesis: The preamble scheduling diff (target emits `sra $v0,$v0,14` after the lui/addiu of %hi/%lo(_ss_score); ours emits it before) and the s5/s4 copy placement may resolve on their own once H5's register split matches, rather than being independent problems.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c list scheduling over the entry block, downstream of the allocation decided in H5
frontier.next_probe: re-run the s6 differ after any H5 fix lands and check whether these three lines disappear before spending a separate probe on them; tools/sched_solver can settle the order question exactly if they do not.
